cards.rueckseite:
- **< 12 h:** often normal; **hyperdense MCA sign**, obscured lentiform nucleus, loss of **insular ribbon**
- **12–24 h:** low density, loss of gray–white differentiation
- **1–3 d:** wedge-shaped hypodensity, mass effect (peaks 3–5 d), possible hemorrhagic transformation
- **4 d – 8 wk:** **gyral enhancement** ("luxury perfusion"), "fogging" at 2–3 weeks
- **Months:** encephalomalacia

cards.vorderseite: DWI/ADC in stroke and other lesions
cards.rueckseite:
Acute infarct: **DWI bright, ADC dark** (restricted diffusion, minutes after onset) for ~7–10 days; later ADC normalizes then becomes bright (T2 shine-through on DWI).
Other restricted lesions: **abscess** (pus), **epidermoid**, highly cellular tumors (**lymphoma**, medulloblastoma), CJD, acute demyelination, status epilepticus.

**Core (infarct):** CBF ↓↓ and **CBV ↓** (rCBF < 30%).
**Penumbra (salvageable):** CBF ↓, **MTT/Tmax ↑**, **CBV normal or ↑** (autoregulatory vasodilation).
Mismatch (large penumbra, small core) selects patients for thrombectomy up to 24 h (DAWN/DEFUSE-3).
cards.notiz: CNBR p. 346; trial data from current guidelines.

cards.rueckseite:
- **Tumor:** **choline ↑** (membrane turnover), **NAA ↓** (neuronal loss), creatine ↓; lactate/lipid in necrotic high grade
- **Abscess:** amino acids (valine, leucine), acetate, succinate, lactate
- **Radiation necrosis:** lipid/lactate, low choline
- **Canavan:** NAA ↑↑
Main use: tumor vs. abscess, tumefactive demyelination, recurrence vs. necrosis.

Both enhance with edema. **Recurrence:** ↑ rCBV on perfusion MRI, ↑ choline/creatine on MRS, FDG-PET/amino acid PET (FET) **hot**, nodular growth.
**Radiation necrosis:** low rCBV, lipid/lactate peak, PET cold, "soap-bubble/Swiss cheese" enhancement, often 6–24 months after RT. **Pseudoprogression:** within 3 months after chemoradiation (more frequent with MGMT methylation).

"**MAGIC DR**": **M**etastasis, **A**bscess, **G**lioblastoma, **I**nfarct (subacute), **C**ontusion, **D**emyelination (incomplete ring), **R**esolving hematoma/**R**adiation necrosis.
Clues: abscess has thin smooth ring, thinner on the ventricular side, **restricted diffusion**; GBM thick irregular ring, crosses corpus callosum; demyelination **open (incomplete) ring**.
**Glioblastoma** ("butterfly glioma"), **lymphoma**, **demyelination** (MS, tumefactive), also metastasis (rare), gliomatosis, Marchiafava–Bignami, trauma (diffuse axonal injury in splenium).

zeilen: Enters and widens the IAC ("ice cream cone"), acute angle with petrous bone, cystic change
Dural tail, broad base, obtuse angle, calcification, hyperostosis, rarely in IAC
CSF-like, insinuating, **DWI bright**, FLAIR incompletely suppressed
Arachnoid cyst (DWI dark), lipoma, trigeminal/facial schwannoma, aneurysm, metastasis, paraganglioma (salt-and-pepper)

cards.rueckseite: **Germ cell tumors (~⅔)**, mostly **germinoma** (young males; engulfs calcification, homogeneously enhancing, restricted diffusion; check AFP/β-hCG). Pineal parenchymal tumors (pineocytoma/blastoma: "exploded" peripheral calcification), tectal glioma (pilocytic, enlarged tectum, aqueductal obstruction), **pineal cyst** (common, < 1 cm, thin rim enhancement), meningioma (falcotentorial), vein of Galen malformation.

- **Foramen of Monro:** colloid cyst, **SEGA** (tuberous sclerosis), central neurocytoma
- **Body/septum:** **central neurocytoma** (young adults), subependymoma
- **Atrium (trigone):** **meningioma** (adults), choroid plexus papilloma (children), metastasis
- **3rd ventricle (anterior):** colloid cyst, craniopharyngioma, glioma, germinoma
- **4th ventricle:** children: medulloblastoma, ependymoma, pilocytic astrocytoma; adults: metastasis, hemangioblastoma, choroid plexus papilloma, subependymoma

cards.vorderseite: Medulloblastoma vs. ependymoma vs. pilocytic astrocytoma (posterior fossa, children)
cards.rueckseite:
**Medulloblastoma:** midline **vermis/roof**, **hyperdense on CT**, **restricted diffusion**, CSF seeding (image whole spine).
**Ependymoma:** **floor** of 4th ventricle, "**toothpaste**" extension through **foramina of Luschka/Magendie** into CPA/cisterna magna, calcification, heterogeneous.
**Pilocytic astrocytoma:** cerebellar **hemisphere**, **cyst with enhancing mural nodule**, low ADC values absent (facilitated diffusion).

**S**arcoid/**S**ellar adenoma, **A**neurysm/**A**rachnoid cyst, **T**eratoma (germ cell)/**T**uberculosis, **C**raniopharyngioma/Rathke cleft cyst, **H**ypothalamic glioma/**H**istiocytosis/**H**amartoma, **M**eningioma/**M**etastasis, **O**ptic glioma, **E**pidermoid/dermoid.
Always exclude **aneurysm** before transsphenoidal surgery.

Normal height: up to ~8 mm (adults), up to 10–12 mm in puberty/pregnancy (convex upper border normal). **Posterior pituitary bright spot** on T1 (vasopressin granules; absent in central DI). Normal stalk < 4 mm, midline.
**Microadenoma** (< 1 cm): **hypoenhancing** relative to the gland on **dynamic early** contrast images. Macroadenoma: "snowman/figure-8" through diaphragma; **Knosp grade** for cavernous sinus invasion.

Extra-axial, broad dural base, **CSF cleft** and displaced cortical vessels, **dural tail**, **hyperostosis** of adjacent bone, calcification (psammomatous), homogeneous enhancement, T2 iso; angiography: **"sunburst"** ECA supply and prolonged **"mother-in-law" blush** (comes early, stays late).

Both: cyst with enhancing mural nodule in the posterior fossa.
**Hemangioblastoma:** adults (VHL), **nodule abuts the pia**, **flow voids**, intense angiographic blush, may be solid in the spinal cord with large syrinx.
**Pilocytic astrocytoma:** children, larger nodule, no flow voids, cyst wall may enhance.

cards.vorderseite: Imaging of subarachnoid hemorrhage and vasospasm
cards.rueckseite:
CT is ~95–100% sensitive within 6 h, declines over days → LP for xanthochromia if CT negative after 6 h. FLAIR shows subacute SAH. **CTA** for aneurysm; **DSA** gold standard (3D rotational).
Vasospasm: days **3–14** (peak 7–10), detected by TCD (MCA velocity > 120 cm/s, **Lindegaard ratio > 3**), CTA/CTP, angiography.
cards.notiz: CNBR ch. 4 vascular; Lindegaard from Greenberg 10th ed.

cards.rueckseite: CT: **hyperdense sinus/cord sign**, **empty delta sign** on contrast CT (enhancing dura around nonenhancing clot in the superior sagittal sinus). Venous infarcts: **not in arterial territories**, **hemorrhagic**, white matter/bilateral parasagittal (SSS) or temporal (transverse sinus/Labbé) or thalamic (deep system). CTV/MRV confirm. Risks: pregnancy, OCP, dehydration, thrombophilia, infection, malignancy.

"**Popcorn**" lesion with mixed-signal core (blood of different ages) and complete **hemosiderin rim** (dark on T2, blooming on GRE/SWI); little enhancement, **angiographically occult**. Often associated with a **developmental venous anomaly** ("caput medusae") which must be preserved. Familial forms (CCM1–3): multiple lesions on SWI.

Shearing at gray–white junction, **corpus callosum (splenium)**, dorsolateral **brainstem**; CT often normal or small petechiae. Best seen on **SWI/GRE** (microhemorrhages) and DWI/FLAIR. Grades (Adams): I hemispheres, II + corpus callosum, III + brainstem. Clinical state worse than CT suggests.

cards.vorderseite: Epidural vs. subdural hematoma on CT
cards.rueckseite:
**EDH:** **biconvex/lentiform**, **does not cross sutures** (dura attached) but can cross the midline/tentorium; swirl sign = active bleeding.
**SDH:** **crescentic**, **crosses sutures**, limited by dural reflections (falx, tentorium). Density: acute hyperdense, ~1–3 weeks isodense (look for effaced sulci, displaced gray–white junction), chronic hypodense, mixed = acute on chronic.

Favor hydrocephalus: **rounded/ballooned frontal and temporal horns**, **narrow mamillopontine distance**, **acute callosal angle** (< 90°, NPH), effaced sulci at the vertex (**DESH**: disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid space hydrocephalus in NPH), **transependymal CSF flow** (periventricular FLAIR hyperintensity), bowing of the corpus callosum.
Atrophy: proportional enlargement of sulci and ventricles.

Orthostatic headache. "**SEEPS**": **S**ubdural fluid/hematomas, **E**nhancement of pachymeninges (diffuse, smooth), **E**ngorged venous sinuses (venous distension sign), **P**ituitary enlargement, **S**agging brain (low tonsils, flattened pons, closed suprasellar cistern). Look for spinal CSF leak or CSF–venous fistula (myelography, decubitus CT myelography); treat with epidural blood patch.

- **HSV encephalitis:** medial temporal/insula/cingulate, bilateral asymmetric, hemorrhagic, sparing basal ganglia
- **Bacterial meningitis:** leptomeningeal enhancement; complications: subdural empyema (crescentic, rim-enhancing, restricted), ventriculitis (ependymal enhancement, layering debris)
- **TB:** basal meningeal enhancement, hydrocephalus, infarcts
- **Toxoplasma:** multiple basal ganglia ring lesions, eccentric target sign
- **PML:** nonenhancing asymmetric subcortical white matter

cards.vorderseite: Chiari I vs. Chiari II on imaging
cards.rueckseite:
**Chiari I:** **tonsils ≥ 5 mm** below the foramen magnum (McRae/basion–opisthion line), peg-like tonsils, crowding; syrinx; short clivus, basilar invagination.
**Chiari II:** small posterior fossa, **low tentorium/torcula**, vermis + 4th ventricle + medulla herniated, **cervicomedullary kink**, **tectal beaking**, large massa intermedia, interdigitating gyri (fenestrated falx), callosal dysgenesis, **lückenschädel**, colpocephaly.

cards.vorderseite: Dandy–Walker spectrum vs. mega cisterna magna vs. arachnoid cyst
cards.rueckseite:
**Dandy–Walker malformation:** cystic 4th ventricle, **vermian hypoplasia with upward rotation**, **enlarged posterior fossa with elevated torcula**, hydrocephalus.
**Mega cisterna magna:** large cisterna magna, **normal vermis and 4th ventricle**, no hydrocephalus.
**Retrocerebellar arachnoid cyst:** mass effect on normal vermis/4th ventricle, scalloping of the occipital bone.

cards.vorderseite: Spine MRI: disk herniation vs. scar vs. infection
cards.rueckseite:
**Recurrent disk:** nonenhancing (peripheral rim only on early images), contiguous with disk space.
**Epidural fibrosis (scar):** **enhances homogeneously** early, retracts the thecal sac toward it.
**Discitis–osteomyelitis:** T2 hyperintense disk, **endplate destruction**, enhancement of disk and adjacent vertebrae, paraspinal/epidural abscess.
**Degenerative Modic type 1:** endplate edema but disk not T2 bright, no destruction.

zeilen: Edema, inflammation (vascularized fibrous tissue); associated with low back pain

cards.vorderseite: Intramedullary vs. intradural extramedullary vs. extradural on myelography/MRI
cards.rueckseite:
**Intramedullary:** cord expanded, subarachnoid space narrowed on all sides.
**Intradural extramedullary:** cord displaced to the opposite side, **ipsilateral subarachnoid space widened** ("meniscus/capping sign").
**Extradural:** dura and cord displaced together, subarachnoid space narrowed ("paintbrush" tapering), epidural fat displaced.
